- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias after recent price spikes; model fails to correct for mean reversion post-peak.
- Model exhibits lagged response to true price drops — often underestimates sharp declines or overestimates slow declines.
- Forecasts tend to plateau or rise gradually after initial spike, while true prices often show sharper, more volatile corrections.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility in the final 5–10 days of forecast horizon, especially when true prices show sudden drops or rebounds.
- Overestimation is more pronounced when historical prices are high (e.g., >90) — model assumes continuation of upward trend.
- Model underestimates price drops following high peaks — fails to recognize “rebound after crash” or “mean reversion after spike” patterns.
- Forecasts often overshoot the true price by 2–5% in the first 5–10 days, then gradually converge — suggesting model lacks early correction mechanism.
- Model does not adjust for seasonality or policy-driven price shocks (e.g., ETS auction changes, regulatory updates) — assumes linear continuation.
